newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar opens weaker in light trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar opens weaker in light trading.

text.p: FORECAST RANGE 1.3780/1.3840 ASIAN CLOSE 1.3808
RESISTANCE 1.3735 SUPPORT 1.3875 HI 1.3828 LO 1.3791
CANADA OPEN 1.3819/24 HI 1.3828 EUROPE OPEN 1.3817
* Canada's dollar opened slightly weaker at C$1.3819 (US$0.7236) in light trading on Friday after a quiet session on overseas markets last night, traders said.
* They said the currency would remain volatile as long as any doubts remained as to whether the governing Liberals would win a parliamentary majority in Canada's June 2 general election.
"The Liberals' chances of forming a majority government on election night next Monday now stand at 50-50," CTV News said.
The last in a series of five daily Reuters-Zogby polls released yesterday had showed support for the Liberals rising to 41.9 percent from 39.7 percent in Wednesday's poll.
Traders said the recurring specter of a Liberal minority government definitely spooks markets.
"That (Angus Reid) was a big poll, and it pushed the dollar into negative territory," one trader said.
"The markets bear out that there is a lot of uncertainty out there," the trader added.
Traders also said the markets would keep an eye on U.S. economic date due to be released this morning.
The U.S Department of Commerce will release its second estimate of first quarter gross domestic product at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.
A Reuters survey of economists predicted 6.0 percent growth versus a 5.6 percent rate in the government's first estimate.
"The markets are clearly predisposed to believing that the Fed will raise rates in July," said Reid Farrill, corporate foreign exchange adviser for CIBC Wood Gundy.
"If there is any sign of inflation, I think the market will really pick up on it," Farrill said.
Overseas, the Canadian dollar continued to gain ground at the expense of weakening European currencies.
The Italian lira and the Spanish peseta were the latest currencies to feel a two-week downdraft sweeping the continent.

Analysts said uncertainty over who would win the second round of French elections on Sunday and a controversial attempt by the German government to revalue central bank assets had forced a move to the U.S. dollar and Swiss franc.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 84.18 yen from Thursday's close of 84.07 yen and firmed to 1.2304 marks from Thursday's 1.2282 marks.
((Paul Simao, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8104))
